text: Let $S=\left \{z=x+iy:\frac{2z-3i}{4z+2i}\mathrm{is}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{real}\mathrm{number}\right \}$. Then which of the following is NOT correct?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that $z=x+iy$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{then}\dfrac{2z-3i}{4z+2i}=\dfrac{2(x+iy)-3i}{4(x+iy)+2i} \\  \\ =\dfrac{2x+i(2y-3)}{4x+i(4y+2)}\times \dfrac{4x-i(4y+2)}{4x-i(4y+2)} \\  \\ =\dfrac{8x^{2}+(2y-3)(4y+2)}{(4x)^{2}+(4y+2)^{2}}+i\left (\dfrac{4x(2y-3)-2x(4y+2)}{(4x)^{2}+(4y+2)^{2}}\right ) \end{array}$

Since, $\frac{2z-3i}{4z+2i}$ is Real $\Rightarrow \mathrm{Img}\left (\frac{2z-3i}{4z+2i}\right )=0$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 4x(2y-3)-2x(4y+2)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2x(4y-6-4y-2)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2x(-8)=0\Rightarrow x=0 \end{array}$

Also, $(4x)^{2}+(4y+2)^{2}\neq 0\Rightarrow y+x^{2}+y^{2}\neq \frac{-1}{4}$

 If $x=0$, then $y\neq -\frac{1}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift

text: Let the number $(22)^{2022}+(2022)^{22}$ leave the remainder $α$ when divided by 3 and $β$ when divided by 7. Then $\left (α^{2}+β^{2}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have, $(22)^{2022}+(2022)^{22}$

As 2022 is completely divisible by 3

So, $(2022)^{22}$ is also divisible by 3

$(22)^{2022}=(21+1)^{2022}=(3\times 7+1)^{2022}=3m+1$

$\Rightarrow (22)^{2022}$ leave a remainder 1 , when divisible by 3 .

$\therefore (22)^{2022}+(2022)^{22}$ leave a remainder 1 when divided by 3

$\therefore α=1$

$\begin{array}{ll} (22)^{2022}+(2022)^{22} & =(21+1)^{2022}+(2023-1)^{22} \\  \\ =7K+1+7μ+1=7(K+μ)+2 \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow (22)^{2022}+(2022)^{22}$ leave a remainder 2 when divisible by 7

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore β=2 \\  \\ \text{Hence,}α^{2}+β^{2}=1^{2}+2^{2}=5 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{g}(x)=f(x)+f(1-x)$ and $f^{''}(x)>0,x\in (0,1)$. If $\mathrm{g}$ is decreasing in the interval $(0,α)$ and increasing in the interval $(α,1)$, then $\tan ^{-1}(2α)+\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{α}\right )+\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{α+1}{α}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have, $g(x)=f(x)+f(1-x)$ 

Differentiating both side, we get 

$g^{'}(x)=f^{'}(x)-f^{'}(1-x)$ 

As $f^{''}(x)>0,f^{'}(x)$ is an increasing function.

Also, $g(x)=f(x)+f(2a-x)$ is always symmetric about $x=a$

So, $g(x)=f(x)+f(1-x)$ is also symmetric about $x=1/2$

$\therefore g$ is decreasing in the interval $(0,1/2)$ and increasing in the interval $(1/2,1)$.

Now,

$\begin{array}{l} \tan ^{-1}2α+\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1}{α}\right )+\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{α+1}{α}\right ) \\  \\ =\tan ^{-1}1+\tan ^{-1}(2)+\tan ^{-1}3=π \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift

text: If the coefficients of $x$ and $x^{2}$ in $(1+x)^{\mathrm{p}}(1-x)^{\mathrm{q}}$ are 4 and $-$5 respectively, then $2p+3q$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have, coefficient of $x$ in $(1+x)^{p}(1-x)^{q}=4$ and 

coefficient of $x^{2}$ in $(1+x)^{p}(1-x)^{q}=-5$

$\begin{array}{l} (1+x)^{p}(1-x)^{q} \\  \\ =\left (1+px+\dfrac{p(p-1)}{2}x^{2}+\ldots \right )\left (1-qx+\dfrac{q(q-1)}{2}x^{2}+\ldots \right ) \\  \\ =1+(p-q)x+\left (\dfrac{p(p-1)}{2}+\dfrac{q(q-1)}{2}-pq\right )x^{2}+\ldots \ldots  \end{array}$

Coefficient of $x$ in $(1+x)^{p}(1-x)^{q}=-q+p$ 

$\Rightarrow p-q=4$ ...........(i)

$\text{Coefficient of}x^{2}\text{in}(1+x)^{p}(1-x)^{q}=\frac{q(q-1)}{2}-pq+\frac{p(p-1)}{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \dfrac{q^{2}-q-2pq+p^{2}-p}{2}=-5 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{p^{2}+q^{2}-2pq-(p+q)}{2}=-5 \\  \\ \Rightarrow (p-q)^{2}-(p+q)=-10 \\  \\ \Rightarrow (4)^{2}-(p+q)=-10[\because \text{From Eq. (i)}] \\  \\ \Rightarrow p+q=26...........(ii) \end{array}$

Form Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $p=15,q=11$ 

$\therefore 2p+3q=2\times 15+3\times 11=30+33=63$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift

text:
Let $f$ be a continuous function satisfying $\int\limits _{0}^{t^{2}}\left (f(x)+x^{2}\right )dx=\frac{4}{3}t^{3},\forall t>0$. Then

$f\left (\frac{π^{2}}{4}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that

$\int\limits _{0}^{t^{2}}\left (f(x)+x^{2}\right )dx=\frac{4}{3}t^{3},\forall t>0$

On differentiating using Leibnitz rule, we get

$\begin{array}{l} \left (f\left (t^{2}\right )+t^{4}\right )\times 2t=\dfrac{4}{3}\times 3t^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow f\left (t^{2}\right )+t^{4}=2t \\  \\ \Rightarrow f\left (t^{2}\right )=2t-t^{4} \end{array}$

On substituting $\frac{π}{2}$ for $t$, we get

$f\left (\frac{π^{2}}{4}\right )=2\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )-\frac{π^{4}}{16}=π\left (1-\frac{π^{3}}{16}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift

text:
For $α,β,γ,δ\in \mathrm{ℕ}$, if $\int \left (\left (\frac{x}{e}\right )^{2x}+\left (\frac{e}{x}\right )^{2x}\right )\log _{e}xdx=\frac{1}{α}\left (\frac{x}{e}\right )^{βx}-\frac{1}{γ}\left (\frac{e}{x}\right )^{δx}+C$

, where $e=\sum\limits _{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{1}{n!}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ is constant of integration, then $α+2β+3γ-4δ$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have, 

$\int \left (\left (\frac{x}{e}\right )^{2x}+\left (\frac{e}{x}\right )^{2x}\right )\log _{e}xdx=\frac{1}{α}\left (\frac{x}{e}\right )^{βx}-\frac{1}{γ}\left (\frac{e}{x}\right )^{δx}+C$

$\begin{array}{ll} \left (\dfrac{x}{e}\right )^{2x} & =\left (\dfrac{e^{\log _{e}x}}{e}\right )^{2x}\left [\because x=e^{\log _{e}x}\right ] \\  \\ =e^{2(x\log _{e}x-x)}.........(i) \end{array}$

$\text{Also,}\left (\frac{e}{x}\right )^{2x}=\left (\frac{x}{e}\right )^{-2x}=e^{-2(x\log _{e}x-x)}$ .........(ii)

Let, 

$\begin{array}{ll} I & =\int \left [\left (\dfrac{x}{e}\right )^{2x}+\left (\dfrac{e}{x}\right )^{2x}\right ]\log _{e}xdx \\  \\ =\int \left [e^{2(x\log _{e}x-x)}+e^{-2(x\log _{e}x-x)}\right ]\log _{e}xdx\text{[From Eqs. (i) and (ii)]} \end{array}$

Let $x\log _{e}x-x=t$

$\log _{e}xdx=dt$

$\begin{array}{ll} I & =\int \left (e^{2t}+e^{-2t}\right )dt=\dfrac{e^{2t}}{2}-\dfrac{e^{-2t}}{2}+C \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}\left (\dfrac{x}{e}\right )^{2x}-\dfrac{1}{2}\left (\dfrac{e}{x}\right )^{2x}+C \end{array}$

On comparing I with $\frac{1}{α}\left (\frac{x}{e}\right )^{βx}-\frac{1}{γ}\left (\frac{e}{x}\right )^{δx}+C$

$\begin{array}{l} α=2,β=2,γ=2,δ=2 \\  \\ \therefore α+2β+3γ-4δ=2+2\times 2+3\times 2-4\times 2=4 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift

Let $μ$ be the mean and $σ$ be the standard deviation of the distribution

  
    $x_{i}$
    0

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have, $\Sigma f_{i}=62$

$\left. \begin{array}{l} (K+2)+2K+\left (K^{2}-1\right )\right )+\left (K^{2}-1\right )+\left (K^{2}+1\right )+(K-3)=62 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 3K^{2}+4K-64=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow (3K+16)(K-4)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow K=4 \end{array}$

$\left (\because k=\frac{-16}{3}\text{is not possible}\right )$

$\begin{array}{llll} x_{i} & f_{i} & f_{i}x_{i} & f_{i}x_{i}^{2} \\ 0 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 8 & 8 & 8 \\ 2 & 15 & 30 & 60 \\ 3 & 15 & 45 & 135 \\ 4 & 17 & 68 & 272 \\ 5 & 1 & 5 & 25 \\ \text{Total} & 62 & 156 & 500 \end{array}$

$μ=\frac{\Sigma f_{i}x_{i}}{\Sigma f_{i}}=\frac{0+8+30+45+68+5}{62}=\frac{156}{62}$

$\begin{array}{ll} σ^{2}= & \dfrac{\Sigma f_{i}x_{i}^{2}}{\Sigma f_{i}}-\left (\dfrac{\Sigma f_{i}x_{i}}{\Sigma f_{i}}\right )^{2} \\  \\ = & \dfrac{1\times 8+4\times 15+9\times 15+16\times 17+25\times 1}{62}-\left (\dfrac{156}{62}\right )^{2} \\  \\ =\dfrac{500}{62}-\left (\dfrac{156}{62}\right )^{2}=\dfrac{500}{62}-μ^{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore σ^{2}+μ^{2}=\dfrac{500}{62} \\  \\ \text{Hence,}\left [σ^{2}+μ^{2}\right ]=8 \end{array}$

text: Let $⃗{a}=2\hat{i}+7\hat{j}-\hat{k},⃗{b}=3\hat{i}+5\hat{k}$ and $⃗{c}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$. Let $⃗{d}$ be a vector which is perpendicular to both $⃗{a}$ and $⃗{b}$, and $⃗{c}\cdot ⃗{d}=12$. Then $(-\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})\cdot (⃗{c}\times ⃗{d})$ is equal to :

text:
If the points $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ are respectively the circumcenter and the orthocentre of a $△\mathrm{ABC}$, then $\mathrm{PA}\leftarrow +\mathrm{PB}\leftarrow +\mathrm{PC}\leftarrow$ is
equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
1. **Circumcenter $P$**:
 

The circumcenter of a triangle is equidistant from the vertices of the triangle. It is the center of the circumcircle, the circle that passes through all three vertices of the triangle.

2. **Orthocenter $Q$**:
 

The orthocenter of a triangle is the point of intersection of its three altitudes. An altitude of a triangle is a perpendicular line segment drawn from a vertex to its opposite side (or its extension).

3. **Centroid $G$**:

The centroid of a triangle is the point of intersection of its medians. A median of a triangle is a line segment joining a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. The centroid always divides each median in a 2:1 ratio, with the larger segment being closer to the vertex.

With the above definitions, it's known that the centroid divides the line segment joining the circumcenter and orthocenter in the ratio 1 : 2, meaning :

$PG\leftarrow =\frac{1}{3}PQ\leftarrow$

$PQ\leftarrow =3PG\leftarrow$
  
The position vector of the centroid $G$ in terms of the vertices $A,B,$ and $C$ is :

$\vec{G}=\frac{\vec{A}+\vec{B}+\vec{C}}{3}$

Because $P$ is the circumcenter and is at the origin in this problem:

$PA\leftarrow =\vec{A}$

$PB\leftarrow =\vec{B}$

$PC\leftarrow =\vec{C}$

Substituting these into the equation for $G$ :

$PG\leftarrow =\frac{PA\leftarrow +PB\leftarrow +PC\leftarrow }{3}$

Now, using the relationship between $PQ$ and $PG$ established earlier :

$PQ\leftarrow =3PG\leftarrow =PA\leftarrow +PB\leftarrow +PC\leftarrow$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift

text: Let A be the point $(1,2)$ and B be any point on the curve $x^{2}+y^{2}=16$. If the centre of the locus of the point P, which divides the line segment $\mathrm{AB}$ in the ratio $3:2$ is the point C$(α,β)$, then the length of the line segment $\mathrm{AC}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have, equation of circle is $x^{2}+y^{2}=16$

Let any point on the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=4^{2}$ is $B(4\cos θ,4\sin θ)$ and $A(1,2)$

Let $\mathrm{P}$ be $(h,k)$ which divides $\mathrm{AB}$ in $3:2$


[IMG]


So

$h=\frac{12\cos θ+2}{3+2}\text{and}k=\frac{12\sin θ+2\times 2}{3+2}$

$\Rightarrow \cos θ=\frac{5h-2}{12}$ and $\sin θ=\frac{5k-4}{12}$

As, $\cos ^{2}θ+\sin ^{2}θ=1,\left (\frac{5h-2}{12}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{5k-4}{12}\right )^{2}=1$

$\Rightarrow \left (h-\frac{2}{5}\right )^{2}+\left (k-\frac{4}{5}\right )^{2}=\frac{12^{2}}{5^{2}}$

$\therefore$ Locus of point $P$ is $\left (x-\frac{2}{5}\right )^{2}+\left (y-\frac{4}{5}\right )^{2}=\frac{12^{2}}{5^{2}}$ 

which is equation of circle with centre $\left (\frac{2}{5},\frac{4}{5}\right )$ 

Hence, $AC=\sqrt{\left (1-\frac{2}{5}\right )^{2}+\left (2-\frac{4}{5}\right )^{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{45}}{5}=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift

text:
Let $\mathrm{A}=\{2,3,4\}$ and $\mathrm{B}=\{8,9,12\}$. Then the number of elements in the relation

$\mathrm{R}=\{((a_{1},\mathrm{b}_{1}),(a_{2},\mathrm{b}_{2}))\in (A\times B,A\times B):a_{1}$ divides $\mathrm{b}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{a}_{2}$ divides $\mathrm{b}_{1}\}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given sets :

$A=\{2,3,4\}$

$B=\{8,9,12\}$

We want to find the number of elements of the form $((a_{1},b_{1}),(a_{2},b_{2}))$ such that :

$a_{1}$ divides $b_{2}$
$a_{2}$ divides $b_{1}$

For the first condition :

$a_{1}$ divides $b_{2}$

Given $a_{1}\in A$ and $b_{2}\in B$, we can list the pairs:

$(a_{1},b_{2})\in \{(2,8),(2,12),(3,9),(3,12),(4,8),(4,12)\}$

This gives 6 pairs.

For the second condition, the pairs are the same, because it's just the reversed relation. So :

$a_{2}$ divides $b_{1}$

Again has 6 valid pairs.

Now, for every pair from the first condition, we can have any pair from the second condition. This leads to :

$6\times 6=36$
relations.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift

text: Let the tangent at any point P on a curve passing through the points (1, 1) and $\left (\frac{1}{10},100\right )$, intersect positive $x$-axis and $y$-axis at the points A and B respectively. If $\mathrm{PA}:\mathrm{PB}=1:k$ and $y=y(x)$ is the solution of the differential equation $e^{\frac{dy}{dx}}=kx+\frac{k}{2},y(0)=k$, then $4y(1)-6\log _{\mathrm{e}}3$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

At $P(x,y)$ the tangent is $Y-y=\dfrac{dy}{dx}(X-x)$. It meets the $x$-axis at $A\left (x-\dfrac{y}{dy/dx},0\right )$ and the $y$-axis at $B\left (0,y-x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right )$.

Since $PA:PB=1:k$, $P$ divides $AB$ internally in the ratio $1:k$, so its abscissa is

$x=\dfrac{k\left (x-\dfrac{y}{dy/dx}\right )+1\times 0}{k+1}\Rightarrow x(k+1)=kx-\dfrac{ky}{dy/dx}\Rightarrow x\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-ky$

Separating variables, $\dfrac{dy}{y}=-k\dfrac{dx}{x}$, so $\ln y=-k\ln x+\ln C$, that is $yx^{k}=C$.

Through $(1,1)$: $C=1$. Through $\left (\dfrac{1}{10},100\right )$: $100\left (\dfrac{1}{10}\right )^{k}=1\Rightarrow 10^{2-k}=1\Rightarrow k=2$.

The differential equation becomes $e^{dy/dx}=2x+1$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\ln (2x+1)$ and, integrating by parts,

$y=x\ln (2x+1)-\int \dfrac{2x}{2x+1}dx=x\ln (2x+1)-x+\dfrac{1}{2}\ln (2x+1)+c$

$y(0)=k=2$ gives $c=2$, so

$y(1)=\ln 3-1+\dfrac{1}{2}\ln 3+2=\dfrac{3}{2}\ln 3+1$

$4y(1)-6\log _{e}3=6\ln 3+4-6\ln 3=4$

Hence, the answer is 4.

text: The sum of all the four-digit numbers that can be formed using all the digits 2, 1, 2, 3 is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have, four digits are $2,1,2,3$.

Total numbers when 1 is at unit digit $=\frac{3!}{2!}=3$

Total number when 2 is at unit digit $=3!=6$

Total numbers when 3 is at unit digit $=\frac{3!}{2!}=3$

Sum of digits at unit place $=3\times 1+6\times 2+3\times 3=24$

$\therefore$ Required sum $=24\times 1000+24\times 100+24\times 10+24\times 1$

$=24\times 1111=26664$

text:
Let $\mathrm{S}$ be the set of values of $λ$, for which the system of equations 

$6λx-3y+3z=4λ^{2}$, 

$2x+6λy+4z=1$, 

$3x+2y+3λz=λ$ has no solution. Then $12\sum\limits _{λ\in S}|λ|$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The system has no solution when $\Delta =0$ and at least one of $\Delta _{x},\Delta _{y},\Delta _{z}$ is non-zero.

$\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 6λ & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & 6λ & 4 \\ 3 & 2 & 3λ \end{array}\right |=6λ(18λ^{2}-8)+3(6λ-12)+3(4-18λ)=108λ^{3}-84λ-24$

$\Delta =0\Rightarrow 9λ^{3}-7λ-2=0\Rightarrow (λ-1)(3λ+1)(3λ+2)=0\Rightarrow λ=1,-\dfrac{1}{3},-\dfrac{2}{3}$.

$\Delta _{z}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 6λ & -3 & 4λ^{2} \\ 2 & 6λ & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & λ \end{array}\right |=-36λ^{3}+16λ^{2}-6λ-9$

At $λ=1$: $\Delta _{z}=-35$; at $λ=-\dfrac{1}{3}$: $\Delta _{z}=-\dfrac{35}{9}$; at $λ=-\dfrac{2}{3}$: $\Delta _{z}=\dfrac{115}{9}$. All are non-zero, so the system has no solution for each of these values.

So $S=\left \{1,-\dfrac{1}{3},-\dfrac{2}{3}\right \}$ and

$12\sum\limits _{λ\in S}|λ|=12\left (1+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{2}{3}\right )=24.$

Hence, the answer is 24.

text: If the domain of the function $f(x)=\sec ^{-1}\left (\frac{2x}{5x+3}\right )$ is $[α,β)\mathrm{U}(γ,δ]$, then $|3α+10(β+γ)+21δ|$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that $f(x)=\sec ^{-1}\left (\frac{2x}{5x+3}\right )$ 

Since, the domain for $\sec ^{-1}x$ is $|x|\geq 1$ 

Therefore $\left |\frac{2x}{5x+3}\right |\geq 1$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{2x}{5x+3}\leq -1\text{or}\dfrac{2x}{5x+3}\geq 1 \\  \\ \dfrac{2x+5x+3}{5x+3}\leq 0\text{or}\dfrac{2x-5x-3}{5x+3}\geq 0 \\  \\ \dfrac{7x+3}{5x+3}\leq 0\text{or}\dfrac{-3(x+1)}{5x+3}\geq 0 \end{array}$

Case I : $7x+3\leq 0$ and $5x+3>0$

$\begin{array}{ll}  & x\leq -\frac{3}{7}\text{or}x>-\frac{3}{5} \\  \\  & \Rightarrow -\frac{3}{5}<x\leq -\frac{3}{7} \end{array}$

Case II : $7x+3\geq 0$ and $5x+3<0$

$x\geq -\frac{3}{7}\text{and}x<-\frac{3}{5}$

Which is not possible

Case III : $x+1\geq 0$ and $5x+3<0$

$\begin{array}{l} x\geq -1\text{and}x<-\dfrac{3}{5} \\  \\ \Rightarrow -1\leq x<-\dfrac{3}{5} \end{array}$

Case IV : $x+1\leq 0$ and $5x+3\geq 0$

$x\leq -1\text{and}x\geq -\frac{3}{5}$

Which is not possible

$\therefore$ Domain is $\left [-1,-\frac{3}{5}\right )\cup \left (-\frac{3}{5},-\frac{3}{7}\right ]$

$\therefore α=-1,β=-\frac{3}{5},γ=-\frac{3}{5},δ=-\frac{3}{7}$

$\therefore$ $|3α+10(β+γ)+21δ|=\left |-3+10\left (-\frac{3}{5}-\frac{3}{5}\right )+21\left (-\frac{3}{7}\right )\right |=24$

text: Let the equations of two adjacent sides of a parallelogram $\mathrm{ABCD}$ be $2x-3y=-23$ and $5x+4y=23$. If the equation of its one diagonal $\mathrm{AC}$ is $3x+7y=23$ and the distance of A from the other diagonal is $\mathrm{d}$, then $50\mathrm{d}^{2}$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
[IMG]


We have, $ABCD$ is a parallelogram

Let equation of $AB$ be $2x-3y=-23\ldots$ (i)

and equation of $BC$ be $5x+4y=23\ldots$ (ii)

Equation of $AC$ is $3x+7y=23\ldots$ (iii)

Solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$x=-1$, and $y=7$

$\therefore$ Co-ordinate of $B$ is $(-1,7)$

On solving Eqs. (ii) and (iii), we get

$x=3,y=2$

$\therefore$ Co-ordinate of $C$ is $(3,2)$

On solving Eqs. (i) and (iii), we get $x=-4$ and $y=5$

$\therefore$ Co-ordinate of $A$ is $(-4,5)$.

Let $E$ be the intersection point of diagonal co-ordinate of 

$E$ is $\left (\frac{-4+3}{2},\frac{5+2}{2}\right )$ or $\left (-\frac{1}{2},\frac{7}{2}\right )$ 

$\because E$ is mid-point of $AC$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Equation of}BD\text{is}y-7=\left (\dfrac{7-\frac{7}{2}}{-1+\frac{1}{2}}\right )(x+1) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 7x+y=0 \end{array}$

Distance of $A$ from diagonal $BD=\frac{|7\times (-4)+5|}{\sqrt{7^{2}+1^{2}}}$

$\therefore d=\frac{23}{\sqrt{50}}$

Hence, $50d^{2}=(23)^{2}=529$
